subject.title: fix(gateway): align runtime config activation with subsystem hot-reload publish (#103736)

question: After the concrete blockers are repaired, should the canonical fix use this commit-late transaction or the publish-early rollback model in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103880?
rationale: Both approaches address the user-visible divergence but establish different permanent gateway lifecycle and rollback semantics that automation should not choose implicitly.

options.title: Commit late atomically
options.body: Keep old state live through deferral and publish only a fully ready replacement under one activation lock.

options.title: Publish early with rollback
options.body: Expose rebuilt subsystems before deferral and restore prior state if a later reload step fails.

recommendation.title: Commit late atomically
recommendation.body: Keep old state live through deferral and publish only a fully ready replacement under one activation lock.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged no-op activation work is the closest established ownership signal for the managed reload and runtime-snapshot boundary.
